projects.title: Xiaohongshu · Follow Along
projects.intro: Helping people move from saved tutorials to hands-on practice and continued discussion. An independent UX design study.

details.description:
I explored how a saved tutorial could lead to hands-on practice and ongoing help from others.

Based on an exploratory review of 18 tutorial posts. Independent design exercise; the proposed flow has not yet been user-tested.

studySections.title: Start with what people already do
studySections.body: I often save tutorials without returning to try them. For this design exercise, I reviewed 18 tutorials across software, crochet, and baking. In the comments, people were already asking questions, answering others, and sharing what they had made. This small exploratory sample suggested supporting those existing exchanges, rather than adding mandatory check-ins.
studySections.bodyZh: 我经常收藏想学的教程，却常常没有下文。这次设计练习中，我查看了软件操作、钩织和烘焙三类共 18 篇教程，发现评论里已经有人提问、回答，也有人分享自己的成果。我希望从这些已有行为出发，让大家更容易开始尝试，也能围绕问题继续交流。这是小样本探索，不代表所有用户的情况。

studySections.title: Where the learning flow breaks
studySections.body: I mapped the path from saving a tutorial to trying it, looking for help, and trying again. Personal experience and examples from the reviewed posts pointed to five possible gaps: starting after saving, adapting a step to a different situation, finding relevant advice, explaining a problem, and knowing whether a suggestion worked. These became design questions to test.
studySections.bodyZh: 我把流程从收藏、重新打开、边看边做，一直梳理到遇到困难、求助和再次尝试。结合个人经历与帖子中的例子，我整理出五个可能的断点：收藏后没有行动、自己的情况与教程不同、找不到适合的经验、难以说清问题，以及给出建议后不知道结果。这些是后续需要验证的设计问题。

studySections.title: Keep practice inside the original note
studySections.body: The concept adds a “Follow Along” mode to a tutorial note. People can jump to the step they need, see discussions attached to that step, and return after trying a suggestion. AI is proposed as support for chapters, reference material, and drafting a question; people review what they post and report whether an answer helped.
studySections.bodyZh: 我在教程笔记里加入“跟着做”：想看哪一步，就看哪一步；卡住时，看看这一步的讨论；试过之后，再回来反馈。AI 帮忙分章节、查资料和整理问题，用户自己检查后发布，再由实际尝试的人说有没有用。

studySections.title: Make the entry easy to find
studySections.body: I designed entry points in the note, full-screen video, and comments, so the proposed flow can start where someone is already watching or asking for help. The entry takes them back to the same tutorial context.
studySections.bodyZh: 我设计了笔记页、全屏视频和评论区三个入口，让用户在正在看教程或找答案的位置进入，并保留原来的教程语境。

studySections.title: Find advice for this particular step
studySections.titleZh: 找到这一步的解决办法
studySections.body: Problem tags lead to related discussions and suggested troubleshooting material. If those do not fit, the person can describe their own situation and ask. The design brings the question, context, and source discussion together; whether this makes useful advice easier to find still needs testing.
studySections.bodyZh: 用户可以从问题标签进入，查看相关讨论和排查建议；如果不适合自己的情况，也可以补充描述再提问。我把问题、教程步骤和来源讨论放在一起，能否帮助用户更快找到适用建议，还需要测试。

studySections.title: Give the exchange a follow-up
studySections.body: People can add text or images to explain where they are stuck, then return to say whether a suggestion worked, keep asking, or share their own approach. The goal is to let a single answer become a continuing exchange around practice.
studySections.bodyZh: 用户可以用文字和图片说明卡在哪里，再回来告诉帮过自己的人有没有解决，也可以继续问，或者分享自己的做法。我希望一次问答能围绕真实尝试继续下去。

studySections.title: Try the idea across different tutorials
studySections.titleZh: 看看它能否用于不同教程
studySections.body: I extended the screens to website building, everyday cooking, video editing, and photography. These are concept scenarios for exploring how the same structure might adapt to different tasks; they are not evidence of adoption.
studySections.bodyZh: 我把界面延展到了网站搭建、日常做菜、视频剪辑和相机拍摄四个场景，用来探索同一套结构如何适应不同任务。这些是设计场景，还不是实际使用结果。

studySections.title: What I need to test next
studySections.body: This is an independent design exercise, not a shipped Xiaohongshu feature. The reviewed posts informed the concept, but I have not yet validated the proposed flow with users. Next, I would test whether people can find Follow Along, connect a problem to the right step, identify the source of advice, and return to give feedback without feeling obliged to check in.
studySections.bodyZh: 这是独立的体验设计练习，并非小红书已上线的功能。帖子观察帮助我形成方案，但拟定流程还没有经过用户测试。接下来，我想验证：用户能否找到入口，把问题对应到正确步骤，辨认建议的来源，以及在不觉得被要求打卡的情况下回来反馈。

projects.title: Descent | Ascent
projects.intro: An autobiographical p5.js game exploring self-perception and choices

details.description: This zine playfully explores the silent, soggy language of divers. Structured as a journey from descent to ascent, it documents how hand gestures become a form of communication when speech disappears underwater. Inspired by real-world diver signaling systems and research in underwater gesture recognition, the project turns practical survival gestures into an unspoken narrative. It’s part observation, part miscommunication, and entirely an ode to talking with your hands when no one can hear you anyway.

projects.title: Mountain Spirit 山鬼
projects.intro: An retro Futuristic Diner built with MAYA

details.description:
Mountain Spirit is an interactive installation inspired by the Chinese mythological figure Shan Gui and Jeremiah 10:3–5. It reflects on how societies create gods—and meaning itself—through shared imagination, belief, and repetition.

They cut a tree from the forest,
a craftsman shapes it with his hands;
they adorn it with silver and gold,
fasten it with nails and hammers so that it will not move.
It stands upright like a palm tree, but cannot speak;
it must be carried because it cannot walk.

projects.title: Autobiographical Game

details.description:
An autobiographical p5.js game I did base on my memory with my dog Xiaowu who passed away years before. It depicts my childhood memory imaging my self as a witch and Xiaowu as my familiar spirit. The visual of the game is inspired by Pixel Jeff. The game used p5.play library to create different scenes and interactions. Players can explore the environment, interact with objects, and experience the story through simple gameplay mechanics.
I miss Xiaowu.

projects.title: Experimental Clock
projects.intro: Data visualization

details.description: For this project, I use the number of ripples to present Hour (12-hour timing since this looks prettier), the number of rings per ripple to represent minutes(using 10 minutes as an interval). To avoid the situation that nothing is shown when the minutes is single digit, the point in the middle represent single digits. For example, if there is 3 points when pressing the mouse, That means it is around 3 AM/PM o'clock, if there is 4 ripples and each ripple has 1 point and 2 rings, that means it's about 4:20 (need to minus the single digit ring). Also, if moving the mouse while pressed, you can fast forward the time or rewind it.

projects.title: Ophelia
projects.intro: A plaster-casting sculpture capturing the ethereal buoyancy of a floating body.

details.description:
Idea: A plaster-casting sculpture that captures the ethereal essence of a floating person. Because whole-body casting is difficult, selected body parts (face and hands) are composed to form a harmonious figure, inspired by the image of a swimmer and the paintings of Ophelia. The piece explores the tension between the solid, tactile texture of plaster and a feeling of weightlessness.

My plaster-casting sculpture showcases select parts of the face and hands in detail to convey beauty and mystery in suspension—where heaviness meets float.

projects.title: Bone Clock
projects.intro: A wearble sculpture

details.description: This wearable sculpture turns my anxiety about time into a physical experience. Laser-cut pieces form a mechanical spine worn on the back, which stiffens and shifts as a clock mechanism moves. As time passes, the structure subtly tightens, echoing the way my own back tenses under pressure. The piece makes the invisible weight of time visible—and felt—on the body.

projects.title: Maternity
projects.intro: Watercolor drawings exploring identity as a mother

details.description: This series of paintings was inspired by my mother. During my high school years, she was struggling to balance her roles as a mother, a wife, and a daughter. My grandfather was suffering from depression, and my grandmother was ill. At the same time, I was going through my college application process and needed her support. Witnessing her efforts to hold everything together deeply moved me, and this work reflects her quiet resilience and the weight of familial responsibility.

projects.title: 'Environmental-Friendly'
projects.intro: Watercolor drawings exploring identity as a mother

details.description: This piece was inspired by the idea of how “environmentally friendly” has become a concept to consume. It appears to be carefully held in a hand, yet it is, in fact, placed on a plate—ready to be consumed.
